text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- The government sets June 15 as the date of the presidential elections.
- Kuna to be introduced in Eastern Slavonia on May 19.

- The National Defence and Security Council holds a session presided over by President Franjo Tudjman and discusses the letter U.S. President Bill Clinton forwarded to the Croatian president on Croat-American relations.
- The Yugoslav dinar cannot endanger the Croatian kuna, which is to become the official currency in Eastern Slavonia as of May 19, claims the deputy Prime Minister, Borislav Skegro.
- An IMF delegation led by Robert Feldman visits the National Bank of Croatia and holds talks with deputy governor Zdravko Rogic.
- Croatian Post and Telecommunications company (HPT) to start working in Eastern Slavonia in line with an agreement signed in Vukovar on Friday.
- Capital market: Foreigners have grabbed all the old savings offered on the Zagreb bourse.
- The candidates in the forthcoming presidential elections have another 12 days to register.

- Students send a note of protest to the Science and Technology Minister Ivica Kostovic stating their dissatisfaction with the work of the ministry and asking for more money to be injected into their projects.

- The ruling Croatian Democratic Union negotiating team and that of the Croatian Social Liberal Party are close to reaching agreement on the set-up of the city administration and the electing of city mayor. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
